class.name: LensFlareElement
class.description: A [LensFlareElement] is a single quad drawn somewhere along the axis that runs from the source, through the centre of the screen, and out the far side. [member position] places it on that axis, which is what makes a flare sweep across the frame as the source moves. [member type] picks between three kinds of element. The first six are evaluated analytically in the shader, so they stay sharp at any resolution and cost no texture memory. The [code]TYPE_BUILTIN_*[/code] entries draw one of the flare textures bundled with the engine, which is what a new flare from [method LensFlare.create_default] is made of; an element that uses one stores only its type in a saved scene, not a copy of the image. [constant TYPE_TEXTURE] draws a [member texture] of your own.

members.member: If [code]true[/code], the element turns to stay aligned with the axis from the source to the centre of the screen, on top of [member rotation]. This is what keeps an anamorphic streak lying across the flare rather than fixed to the screen.
How the element is combined with the image behind it.
Spreads the red, green and blue channels radially about the element's own centre, giving it a coloured fringe. [code]0.0[/code] disables it.
How many copies of the element to draw, each [member spacing] further along the axis than the last. Use it for a run of iris ghosts without authoring each one.

Shapes the element's profile. It softens the edge of a [constant TYPE_DISC] or [constant TYPE_POLYGON], sets the width of a [constant TYPE_RING], tightens the core of a [constant TYPE_GLOW], thins a [constant TYPE_STREAK] and sharpens the spikes of a [constant TYPE_STARBURST]. Ignored by [constant TYPE_TEXTURE] and the built-in textures, which have whatever profile they were drawn with.
Multiplies the element's brightness, on top of [member LensFlare3D.intensity].

Where the element sits on the axis from the source to the centre of the screen. [code]0.0[/code] is on the source, [code]1.0[/code] is the centre of the screen and [code]2.0[/code] is the same distance out the far side. Values outside that range are allowed.
A fixed rotation applied to the element, added to the one [member auto_rotate] works out.
Number of sides of a [constant TYPE_POLYGON], or number of spikes of a [constant TYPE_STARBURST]. Six matches a common camera iris. Ignored by every other shape.
The element's size, as a fraction of the screen's height on both axes, so a round element stays round whatever the aspect ratio.
How far apart the copies made by [member count] sit along the axis. Has no effect when [member count] is [code]1[/code].

The texture drawn when [member type] is [constant TYPE_TEXTURE]. Its alpha and its luminance are multiplied together to get the element's coverage, so a greyscale flare texture with no alpha channel works as well as a cut out one.

If [code]true[/code], the element is also multiplied by [member LensFlare3D.color], so one flare resource follows the colour of whatever light it is attached to. Turn it off for an element whose colour is part of the flare's look, such as a blue anamorphic streak.

constants.constant: A soft radial falloff. Use it on the source itself for the bloom around a bright light.
A filled circle with a soft rim, the plain round ghost thrown by a circular aperture.
An annulus, for the halo that rings a bright source.
A filled regular polygon with [member sides] sides, the ghost thrown by a bladed iris.
A horizontal bar with a soft falloff, the anamorphic streak an oval lens element throws.
A core with [member sides] spikes radiating from it, thrown by a stopped down iris.
The [member texture], drawn as is. Use it for elements the procedural shapes cannot produce.
A bright core shot through with fine rays. Sits on the source.
A starburst with long, uneven rays. Sits on the source.
A plain soft round glow, the photographed counterpart to [constant TYPE_GLOW].
A ghost with the internal structure a real iris throws.
A filled hexagonal iris ghost.
A hollow hexagonal iris ghost.
A soft round ghost.
A thin ring, for the halo around a bright source.
A twin lobed streak. Give it a wide, short [member size] and turn on [member auto_rotate] for an anamorphic flare.
Represents the size of the [enum Type] enum.
Adds the element to the image behind it. This is how stray light actually behaves and is the right choice for nearly every element.
Screens the element over the image behind it, which saturates less on top of an already bright background.
Represents the size of the [enum BlendMode] enum.
